title: CCTV off, phone purged: Bengaluru cops probe killing of child who saw dad’s murder
content: Police arrested Harini for allegedly killing her husband and son. She reportedly conspired with her lover, Vinay, to commit the murders. The child was allegedly strangled after witnessing his father's death. Investigators suspect property was a motive for the alleged double murder. Harini confessed to the killings during police interrogation.

title: ‘Protest hasn't ended’: Devendra Mahto announces 2nd phase of Jharkhand exam stir

He announced a second phase of protest demanding corruption-free recruitment through JPSC and JSSC. The agitation will continue until the government guarantees no future paper leaks or irregularities. The government has formed an exam reforms committee to strengthen the recruitment process.

title: US insurance giant CEO to business leaders: Look beyond your AI obsession
content: Thomas J. Wilson, CEO of Allstate, emphasizes the urgency for companies to invest in quantum research now. He asserts that quantum computing holds the key to tackling intricate challenges beyond the reach of conventional computers. Firms that embrace this emerging technology early will secure a distinct competitive edge. Establishing essential knowledge and infrastructure for quantum systems is crucial.

title: 'We don't share girlfriends!': Inside the lives of badminton's sibling partnerships
content: At the BWF World Championships in Delhi, sibling partnerships offer more than a shared surname. Scotland’s identical Grimley twins have spent two decades learning each other’s game, while France’s Popov brothers see doubles as an escape from the pressures of singles. Czech siblings Ondrej and Jiri Kral, meanwhile, embrace the comfort, and occasional friction, of sharing life and badminton.

title: JSSC-CGL exam cancellation ends one protest, sparks another as 2,000 fear job loss

They fear losing their government jobs after the cancellation announcement on Monday night.  Protesters demanded a CBI probe and an opportunity to defend themselves against allegations.  The government defended the cancellation to restore confidence in the recruitment system.  Fresh vacancies will provide opportunities for deserving candidates after reforms.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her approach allows acquiring and erasing patient debt at steep discounts. This model has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar initiatives. While philanthropic efforts provide immediate relief, policy reform remains stalled. Lasting change may require systemic reforms addressing the root causes of medical debt.

title: Goa night club fire: Bombay HC cancels bail of Luthra brothers and Ajay Gupta

The state challenged lower court bail orders in the fire and forgery cases. Investigations revealed the club lacked essential fire safety and had an illegal structure. The accused denied responsibility, blaming an event company for the fire.

title: Google buys a dead airline's data for $10 million, but here's what it's not getting
content: Google has won a bankruptcy auction for Spirit Airlines' internal business data with a $10 million bid, beating AI firm Mercor, and says the trove will help train its AI models. The company clarified it is not buying customer or credit card information. Filings list 100 million emails, 500 million Teams chats and 30 million lines of code. A judge considers the Spirit Airlines data sale on August 19.

title: Dia Mirza on co-stars: Recalls feeling safe with Madhavan; praises Salman, Bachchan

She called Jimmy Sheirgill "ever-evolving," recalled feeling safe with R Madhavan during her debut at 19, praised Amitabh Bachchan's discipline, and called Salman Khan "the most generous" person she's worked with. She was last seen in Operation Safed Sagar.

title: Why Manhattan’s Flatiron Building is suddenly one of its hottest luxury addresses
content: New York's Flatiron Building is becoming a sought-after luxury residential address. Most apartments are already under contract as the landmark prepares for resident move-ins. A $24 million apartment recently entered contract, highlighting strong buyer interest. The century-old building is undergoing a significant conversion from offices to upscale homes. Residents will enjoy modern amenities after the building's completion this autumn.

title: David Warner convicted of drink-driving; Big Bash captaincy under cloud
content: On Easter Sunday, David Warner, ex-Australian cricketer, was penalised and ordered to install an interlock device after being convicted of mid-range drink-driving during a random breath test. The court acknowledged the significant media attention and economic consequences he might face. However, the judge highlighted the critical aspect of deterrence with children present in the vehicle.

title: No chemistry teacher: Gen alpha students protest at Azamgarh school
content: Students protested their Azamgarh college, citing excessive fees and teacher shortages. They demanded a chemistry teacher, receiving assurances of one within forty-eight hours. Allegations of unreturned funds and management issues were also raised by supporters. The students seek fair treatment and better academic facilities from the institution. They warned of renewed protests if the chemistry teacher is not provided promptly.

title: Banks closed tomorrow: Why branches will remain shut in Tripura on August 19
content: On August 19, banks across Tripura will be closed in observance of a regional holiday. Other states will also experience bank holidays later this month to honor various festivals. While branch operations will be halted, digital banking services will continue to function normally. Customers should adjust their plans accordingly to account for these closures while still being able to access online and ATM banking throughout the holidays.

title: ‘He quit his job’: Unnati’s emotional tribute to father after World C'ships debut win

She expressed heartfelt thanks to her father, who sacrificed his career to coach her diligently. Inspired by Ayush Shetty's surprising triumph over a top competitor, Unnati is determined to focus on her performance and give her best throughout the tournament.

title: Indore student fails JEE twice, builds Rs 2 lakh freelance career; Warikoo reacts
content: Ankur Warikoo’s post about an Indore-based designer who failed JEE twice before building a successful freelance career has sparked debate over India’s obsession with educational credentials. While Warikoo argues that talent often remains hidden behind college labels, critics say such success stories are exceptions. The discussion highlights the need to assess ability beyond degrees and prestigious institutions.

title: Rishabh Pant creates history, becomes first Indian to achieve this feat
content: India's star wicketkeeper batter Rishabh Pant created history on Tuesday during the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. The India wicketkeeper-batter became the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket. Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty.

title: Why India is considering sugar imports as prices hit record levels
content: India is considering limited duty-free sugar imports and tighter stock limits. These measures aim to boost domestic supplies and control record high sugar prices. Wholesale sugar prices have climbed nearly twenty percent since early August. Festival season demand typically increases sweetener consumption sharply each year. The government is examining several policy options to manage market conditions.

title: Delhi researchers worry over mosquitoes that survived powerful insecticide
content: A recent study from the University of Delhi reveals that mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti, may be becoming less susceptible to the widely-used insecticide alpha-cypermethrin. Laboratory results indicate a small reduction in the insecticide's effectiveness, and researchers discovered specific enzymes aiding in its breakdown. These findings underscore the necessity for diverse mosquito management techniques to ensure continued success in pest control efforts.

title: Video: VCK protest turns violent after TN cop slaps passing man, he retaliates

The man retaliated by slapping the officer back during the heated exchange.  Police intervened and forcibly arrested the man after he refused to cooperate.  Authorities stated minimal force was used to contain the situation and prevent escalation.

title: Hingoli ZP school headmaster accused of being drunk in classes suspended

Complaints poured in from students and parents regarding his lack of proper class management. His unsatisfactory answers to the show-cause notice led to this suspension order, sparked by a campaign initiated by Abhijeet Dipke in Hingoli. He is now subject to disciplinary actions governed by Maharashtra Zilla Parishad rules.

title: Death penalty by lethal injection, shooting or electrocution? SC rejects plea

The court permitted the Centre to form an expert panel.  This panel will examine alternative execution methods for reduced pain.  Hanging remains the current method while reviews are pending.

title: Bangladesh does not want Teesta dispute to hurt ties with India, says minister
content: The Teesta begins in the Himalayas and flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh. It eventually joins the Jamuna, which is the Bangladeshi name for the Brahmaputra. The river is particularly important to northern Bangladesh, where farmers depend on its water. It is also important to West Bengal for irrigation and power generation, with several districts in North Bengal relying on its waters.

title: IAS officer who helped turn India's software industry into global powerhouse
content: N Vittal, the IAS officer and former Secretary of the Department of Electronics, played a key role in shaping India's software industry by removing regulatory barriers and promoting shared digital infrastructure. The article traces how a 1985 Texas Instruments satellite link, famously transported by bullock cart in Bengaluru, demonstrated India's potential for global software exports. Vittal later championed Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), helping companies access communication infrastructure, hardware and global markets while accelerating India's IT revolution.

title: India eyes first cargo ship along Arctic Route to Russia - why it matters

The NSR stretches about 5,600 km across Russia’s Arctic waters. Much of the route remains covered by thick ice for most of the year.

content: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant says that notice has been issued in all petitions; he asks advocates to submit suggestions by the evening for the ambit of the high-powered committee to investigate the police excesses during the protests

title: Naidu reviews search for boat with eight fishermen missing off Konaseema
content: The boat set out from the Odalarevu jetty on August 3 and was expected back by August 12; the Chief Minister asked the Coast Guard, the Fisheries Department and the district administration to keep searching until it is traced

title: Dabholkar murder: Bombay HC grants bail to convict Sachin Andure, suspends his life sentence
content: Dabholkar's daughter Mukta had filed an appeal before the Bombay HC challenging the acquittals in the case and the exclusion of UAPA charges against Andure and Kalaskar; she alleged in her plea that the murder was part of a larger conspiracy by right-wing extremists.

title: Chandy Oommen defends NSS chief Sukumaran Nair amid criticism
content: Congress MLA calls NSS general secretary an 'asset' to Keralam. The remarks follow sharp criticism directed at Nair by Kerala Congress (B) leader K.B. Ganesh Kumar

title: Tamil Nadu government plans to offer ₹10 lakh each to families of three Tamils killed in Karnataka forest
content: To a question from DMK member and former Chief Minister O. Panneerselvam on who fired first, the Forest Minister said the magisterial inquiry would reveal every detail.

title: Russia warns UK over Ukraine drone supplies, says Britain will face ‘consequences’
content: ANI Russia warns Britain it will pay a 'price' for its support for Ukraine . embassy in London accuses the country of 'deliberately opting for an escalation' the warning follows reports in the Times and Sunday Times that British-made drones had been used by Ukraine in long-range strikes .

title: Cyprus grape helps Australian vineyards cope with extreme heat and use less water
content: Xynisteri, a venerable white grape of Cyprus, is proving remarkably resilient in conditions which are putting increasing stress on conventional wine grapes . some growers using the variety have cut water consumption by as much as 75 per cent, with the vines continuing to withstand extreme heat .

title: Blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children; UN condemns 'heinous' act
content: a hand grenade explosion near school in dasht-e-Barchi injured at least 50 children . local media reports put the number of injured at around 50 children, though the figure has not been independently verified . the blast occurred around 4.30pm local time near the school, with several injured students taken to a nearby hospital .

title: Webb's 'little red dots' puzzled astronomers; this galaxy may hold the answer

title: PM CARES Fund data made public; balance rises to Rs 8,452 crore
content: the PM CARES Fund recorded total receipts of Rs 8,452.95 crore in the financial year 2024-25 . fixed deposits accounted for nearly 93 per cent of the fund's closing balance . interest earned from these fixed deposits stood at Rs 469.38 crore .

title: Bihar transfers 17 IPS officers amid row over AK-47 use during student protest
content:
The constable, Abhishek Kumar, has been suspended and faces departmental proceedings

NEW DELHI: Bihar government on Tuesday transferred 17 IPS officers, including the superintendents of police in Bhojpur and Siwan, where police action during recent student protests had sparked controversy. The development comes as the state government told the Supreme Court that a constable fired four rounds from an AK-47 in the air after being surrounded by protesters in Siwan on July 25. The government said no protester was injured in the firing, though three others suffered minor firearm injuries during police action that day. The constable, Abhishek Kumar, has been suspended and faces departmental proceedings. The government said the rifle was meant for special operations, not routine crowd control.This is a developing story. Details to follow...

title: 'This is the right way': Rahul welcomes end of Jharkhand students’ hunger strike
content: leader of opposition in Lok Sabha calls for changes to the existing system . he says he stood with every student in the country and called for changes . the students had exercised restraint and made their concerns heard, he said .

title: 'Got trapped in crowd': Bihar govt defends constable who fired AK-47 during protests
content: a constable deployed during student protests in Siwan fired four rounds from an AK-47 only after he was "trapped and surrounded by protesters" the government said the firing was directed into the air and did not injure any protesters . affidavit says the incident took place near JP Chowk in siwan .

title: 'Move Imran Khan to hospital': Pakistan SC directs govt amid ex-PM's health concerns
content: imran Khan, 73, has been in jail since august 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he and his supporters have described as politically motivated . his party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier . he should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied .
